fwer_statement: Two Holm families, one per primary, each at its family-wise error rate (m fixed at the registered arm count). Across both families the family-wise error rate can reach 0.10 (the Bonferroni bound over two families), and this report states it. Defaults read only the decisional family (at most 0.05). The guards can only veto a rejection, so they never raise the error rate.

preregistration.default_rule: Applied by hand in EXPERIMENT-S2.md, never by code (D-252). Candidates: deepseek (the carried reference arm), haiku-5.5 and sonnet-5.5. A Claude reader is eligible iff its null guard passes; a failed or not-evaluable guard removes it. deepseek is the guard's reference, has no guard of its own and stays eligible (D-270a). Every arm answers each question 5 times; a question's score is its mean answer_usable over the 5, and every test is the exact sign-flip permutation on the per-question mean differences (D-274). Reader choice: the eligible reader with the lowest cost per answered question (sync list price x tokens over all 5 answers, reader_comparison, D-257) is the starting pick and wins, unless a dearer eligible reader is significantly better on answer_usable than it: every pair of eligible readers is tested on its own population (reader_comparison pairs), Holm runs once over all those pairs at alpha 0.05, and a dearer reader whose pair with the pick Holm rejects with a positive delta is significantly better. Then the pick steps up to the cheapest such reader and the check repeats against the readers dearer than it; the pick no dearer reader beats wins (D-275, amending D-270b). A pick of the cheapest reads 'no larger difference detected', not equivalence: the smallest detectable effect is about 0.084 (8.4 points). opus-5.5 is a descriptive arm, run unconditionally beside the other two: reported with its paired delta and cost per answered question, outside the winner rule and the Holm family (D-267). Default-model switch (D-245): Lancet's default generation model may change from deepseek to haiku-5.5 iff the haiku-5.5 row is not significantly worse (Holm over this family, m = 2, alpha 0.05, does not reject it with a negative delta; D-268), its point estimate is at least -0.03, its null guard passes, and its cost per answered question is below deepseek's; a separate product decision with its own reading. p-values are reported, not used, except in the reader choice's and that switch's Holm tests

reader_comparison.cost_basis: Every reader is scored on the same G questions: the ones every reader of the group is ok on (a reader replaying a rerank-degraded context is dropped with its base). cost per answered question = sync list price x the reader's tokens over those questions, divided by its answer_usable answers among them; the retrieval every reader shares is left out. The batch spend is the reader's actual usage at the batch rate (0.5 x the sync price), apart from the comparison.
